accepted.s: In which month and year was the defence sector opened to Indian private participation with foreign direct investment up to 26 per cent under licensing?
accepted.x: The defence sector was opened to 100 per cent Indian private participation in May 2001, with FDI up to 26 per cent under the licensing route.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of a date and policy change.

accepted.s: With reference to foreign direct investment in the defence sector, which one of the following is correct?
o: 100 per cent FDI is permitted through the automatic route for all defence activities.
74 per cent FDI is permitted only through the government route and investment above it is not allowed.
26 per cent is permitted through the automatic route and any higher investment is prohibited.
74 per cent is permitted through the automatic route, while investment above 74 per cent up to 100 per cent requires the government route in cases involving access to modern technology.
accepted.x: The current provision allows 74 per cent FDI through the automatic route. Investment above 74 per cent and up to 100 per cent requires the government route where modern technology access is involved.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between automatic and government routes and their limits.

accepted.s: The cumulative FDI received in the defence sector from May 2001 to June 2025 was approximately:
accepted.x: Cumulative defence-sector FDI from May 2001 to June 2025 amounted to ₹5,730.55 crore.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of a cumulative figure.

accepted.s: Since 2013–14, how many defence licences have been issued to private firms?
accepted.x: Since 2013–14, 576 defence licences have been issued to private firms.
accepted.tq: Number-based elimination using closely spaced figures.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding defence production and exports:
1. Defence production in FY 2024–25 reached ₹1,51,339 crore.
2. Defence production in FY 2025–26 reached a record ₹1.78 lakh crore.
3. Defence exports increased from ₹686 crore in 2013–14 to ₹23,622 crore in 2024–25.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Production reached ₹1,51,339 crore in FY 2024–25 and ₹1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025–26, while exports rose from ₹686 crore to ₹23,622 crore over the stated period.
accepted.tq: Combine production and export figures before selecting the coded option.

accepted.s: The rise in India’s defence exports from ₹686 crore in 2013–14 to ₹23,622 crore in 2024–25 represents approximately:
accepted.x: The increase is described as approximately 34-fold over the period from 2013–14 to 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Quantitative recall of a comparative growth figure.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the DPEPP 2020 targets for 2025?
o: ₹1.75 lakh crore production and ₹35,000 crore exports
₹1.50 lakh crore production and ₹30,000 crore exports
₹1.25 lakh crore production and ₹25,000 crore exports
₹2.00 lakh crore production and ₹50,000 crore exports
accepted.x: DPEPP 2020 set a target of ₹1.75 lakh crore in defence production and ₹35,000 crore in defence exports by 2025.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of paired policy targets.

accepted.s: An older formulation associated with the DPEPP 2020 target referred to a turnover of:
accepted.x: The older formulation referred to $25 billion turnover, including $5 billion in exports.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an older target formulation from the rupee-denominated target.

accepted.s: The defence R&D budget for FY 2026–27 is:
accepted.x: The defence R&D budget for FY 2026–27 is ₹29,100 crore.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of a budget allocation.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about India’s defence-export position is correct?
o: India is outside the top 25 arms exporters but produces all its defence chips domestically.
India is outside the top 25 arms exporters and continues to import jet engines and defence chips.
India is the world’s largest arms exporter but imports only small arms.
India is among the top ten arms exporters and does not import jet engines.
accepted.x: Despite record exports, India remains outside the top 25 arms exporters and imports jet engines and defence chips.
accepted.tq: Use the precise comparison and the linked import constraint.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to recent defence-export developments?
accepted.x: The Philippines is associated with BrahMos, Indonesia with Astra, and the UAE was in talks with India.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure buyer-product pair and verify the remaining associations.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ministry of Defence signed 193 contracts worth ₹2,09,050 crore in 2024–25.
2. Domestic industry received 92 per cent of these contracts.
3. The entire value of the contracts was reserved exclusively for public-sector undertakings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The contracts were not reserved exclusively for public-sector undertakings; 92 per cent went to domestic industry.
accepted.tq: Reject the extreme word “entirely” and retain the supported numerical statements.

accepted.s: In 2021, the Ordnance Factory Board was reorganised by dissolving it and regrouping its factories into:
accepted.x: The 200-year-old OFB was dissolved in 2021, and its 41 factories were regrouped into seven DPSUs.
accepted.tq: Test the linked count of factories and successor DPSUs.

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the seven DPSUs formed after the dissolution of the Ordnance Factory Board?
accepted.x: The seven DPSUs included Munitions India, AVNL, AWEIL, Troop Comforts, Yantra India, India Optel and Gliders India. Bharat Electronics Limited was not one of them.
accepted.tq: Find the one organisation outside the specified successor group.

accepted.s: The BEL defence systems integration complex at Palasamudram is located in:
accepted.x: BEL Palasamudram is located in Sri Sathya Sai district and is intended for integration of missile and radar systems.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between Andhra Pradesh defence locations.

accepted.s: The principal purpose of the BEL complex at Palasamudram is the integration of:
o: Aircraft engines and jet fuel systems
accepted.x: The Palasamudram complex is BEL’s defence systems integration complex for missile and radar systems.
accepted.tq: Match an establishment with its specialised function.

accepted.s: Rambilli in Anakapalli district is associated with which of the following defence facilities?
o: A submarine construction yard operated by Goa Shipyard
A DRDO naval weapons laboratory for torpedoes only
A BEL complex for radar integration
A new Eastern Naval Command base for submarines, including nuclear-powered boats
accepted.x: The naval base at Rambilli, near Visakhapatnam, is intended as a new Eastern Naval Command base for submarines, including nuclear boats.
accepted.tq: Identify the facility from its location and operational purpose.

accepted.s: Which of the following activities is associated with NSTL, Visakhapatnam?
o: Development of torpedoes such as Varunastra, mines and autonomous underwater vehicles
Manufacture of defence chips for export
Production of stealth frigates and destroyers
Integration of fighter aircraft and flight testing only
accepted.x: NSTL is DRDO’s naval weapons laboratory, associated with torpedoes such as Varunastra, mines and AUVs.
accepted.tq: Link a specialised laboratory with its weapons and systems.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
1. ADA Aircraft Integration & Flight Testing Complex — Sri Sathya Sai district
2. Bharat Forge MGT facility — Visakhapatnam
3. DRDO testing range — near Kurnool
4. BDL and Kalyani units — Andhra Pradesh defence ecosystem
accepted.x: All four associations are correct. The ADA complex is in Sri Sathya Sai district, Bharat Forge’s MGT facility is at Visakhapatnam, the DRDO range is near Kurnool, and BDL and Kalyani also have units in the state.
accepted.tq: Combine multiple location-purpose pairs and select the complete set.

accepted.s: The approximate value associated with the ADA Aircraft Integration & Flight Testing Complex in Sri Sathya Sai district is:
accepted.x: The ADA Aircraft Integration & Flight Testing Complex is associated with an investment of ₹15,803 crore.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of a project-cost figure.

accepted.s: INS Vikrant was commissioned by the Prime Minister at Cochin Shipyard on:
accepted.x: INS Vikrant was commissioned by the Prime Minister at Cochin Shipyard on 2 September 2022.
accepted.tq: Recall the commissioning date and venue together.

accepted.s: Project-75 relates to:
o: AIP-equipped submarines developed with Spain’s Navantia alone
Stealth destroyers of the Visakhapatnam class
Nilgiri-class stealth frigates built by MDL and GRSE
Scorpene or Kalvari-class submarines built with France’s Naval Group at MDL
accepted.x: Project-75 concerns Scorpene, or Kalvari-class, submarines constructed at MDL with France’s Naval Group.
accepted.tq: Separate Project-75 from Project-75(I) and the surface-ship projects.

accepted.s: INS Vaghsheer is the:
o: Fourth and last destroyer of Project 15B
Sixth and last submarine of Project-75
Seventh and last frigate of Project 17A
Second and last submarine of Project-75
accepted.x: INS Vaghsheer is the sixth and last Project-75 Scorpene-class submarine, associated with 2025.
accepted.tq: Use project number and platform sequence to avoid class confusion.

accepted.s: Khanderi and Vagir are respectively the:
o: Second and fifth Project-75 Kalvari-class submarines
accepted.x: Khanderi is the second and Vagir the fifth Project-75 Kalvari-class submarine.
accepted.tq: Test ordinal positions within the same project rather than the ship names alone.
accepted.sec: Indigenous warships and submarine projects → class/project  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Project-75(I) is associated with which of the following arrangements?
o: AIP-equipped conventional submarines and a Navantia–L&T teaming agreement
Stealth frigates and a Russia–L&T agreement
Nuclear submarines and a France–GRSE agreement
Aircraft carriers and a Spain–MDL agreement
accepted.x: Project-75(I) concerns next-generation conventional submarines with air-independent propulsion, with Navantia of Spain and L&T signing a teaming agreement in July 2023.
accepted.tq: Separate the project’s propulsion feature, partners and platform type.
accepted.sec: Indigenous warships and submarine projects → class/project  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Indian naval ship projects:
1. Project 17A consists of seven Nilgiri-class stealth frigates.
2. Project 15B includes INS Imphal.
3. INS Surat is the fourth and last ship of Project 15B.
4. Project 17A consists of seven stealth destroyers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Project 17A consists of Nilgiri-class stealth frigates, whereas Project 15B consists of stealth destroyers; therefore statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Catch the reversed comparison between frigates and destroyers.
accepted.sec: Indigenous warships and submarine projects → class/project  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Project 17A is correct?
o: INS Mahendragiri was the second ship and was built entirely outside India.
All seven ships were commissioned before 2022.
Project 17A comprises six submarines constructed only at MDL.
Nilgiri, Udaygiri and Himgiri were delivered in 2025; Taragiri was the fourth ship and Mahendragiri the seventh.
accepted.x: Nilgiri, Udaygiri and Himgiri were delivered in 2025; Taragiri is the fourth ship and INS Mahendragiri is the seventh ship of Project 17A.
accepted.tq: Use sequence and status details to identify the precisely worded statement.
accepted.sec: Indigenous warships and submarine projects → class/project  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes INS Mahendragiri?
o: The fifth Project-75 submarine commissioned in France
The fourth and last Project 15B destroyer commissioned at Russia
The first indigenous aircraft carrier commissioned in 2022
The seventh Project 17A ship, sixth commissioned, associated with the Eastern Fleet and more than 75 per cent indigenous content
accepted.x: INS Mahendragiri is the seventh Project 17A ship, the sixth to be commissioned, associated with the Eastern Fleet and having more than 75 per cent indigenous content.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among platform number, commissioning sequence and indigenous content.
accepted.sec: Indigenous warships and submarine projects → class/project  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Tavasya is associated with which of the following?
o: An indigenously built stealth frigate launched by the Navy, belonging to the P-1135.6 follow-on project at Goa Shipyard
A Nilgiri-class frigate constructed at GRSE under Project 17A
A Scorpene submarine built at MDL under Project-75
A Kamorta-class corvette built at Cochin Shipyard
accepted.x: Tavasya is an indigenously built stealth frigate launched by the Navy, associated with the P-1135.6 follow-on project at Goa Shipyard.
accepted.tq: Identify the platform from its project, yard and class description.
accepted.sec: Indigenous warships and submarine projects → class/project  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Commissioning of INS Vikrant
B. Navantia–L&T teaming agreement for Project-75(I)
C. Commissioning of INS Tamal
D. Delivery of the initial three Project 17A ships in 2025
accepted.x: INS Vikrant was commissioned in September 2022, the Navantia–L&T agreement was signed in July 2023, the three Project 17A ships were delivered in 2025, and INS Tamal was commissioned on 1 July 2025.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence using the two dated events before ordering the 2025 developments.
accepted.sec: Indigenous warships and submarine projects → class/project  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements is correct regarding naval inductions in 2025?
o: INS Tamal was India’s first indigenous aircraft carrier commissioned at Cochin Shipyard.
INS Tamal was the seventh Project 17A ship commissioned at Visakhapatnam.
The Navy commissioned only four vessels, all built in France, in 2025.
The Navy commissioned 12 ships and submarines, including INS Tamal as the last foreign-built vessel, in Russia on 1 July 2025.
accepted.x: The Navy commissioned 12 ships and submarines in 2025. INS Tamal, commissioned in Russia on 1 July 2025, was the last foreign-built vessel.
accepted.tq: Combine the overall count with the distinctive exception of a foreign-built vessel.
accepted.sec: Indigenous warships and submarine projects → class/project  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Project 28 — Kamorta-class anti-submarine warfare corvettes
2. Kiltan — Project 28
3. Mahe class — anti-submarine shallow-water craft
4. Malvan and Agray — Mahe-class craft
accepted.x: All four associations are correct. Project 28 includes Kamorta-class ASW corvettes such as Kiltan, while Malvan and Agray are associated with Mahe-class ASW shallow-water craft.
accepted.tq: Verify each class, project and example before choosing the complete combination.

accepted.s: The principal purpose of the Technology Development Fund is to:
o: Provide grants to industry, especially MSMEs and start-ups, for defence technology development under Make in India
Provide pensions to personnel of the armed forces
Fund only the construction of naval bases by public-sector undertakings
Finance only the import of completed foreign defence systems
accepted.x: TDF provides grants to industry, with particular emphasis on MSMEs and start-ups, to support indigenous defence technology development.
accepted.tq: Apply the scheme’s beneficiary and purpose to an institutional scenario.
accepted.sec: Technology Development Fund - purpose, cap, projects  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The maximum funding available as a grant under the Technology Development Fund for a project is:
accepted.x: TDF provides funding of up to ₹50 crore per project as a grant.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of the scheme’s funding cap.
accepted.sec: Technology Development Fund - purpose, cap, projects  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the TDF-supported green propulsion system?
o: It was developed by Navantia and tested on a Project-75(I) submarine in July 2023.
It was developed by BEL and tested at the Rambilli naval base in 2025.
It was developed by NSTL and tested on INS Vikrant in September 2022.
It was developed by Bellatrix Aerospace and tested in space on PSLV-C58 in January 2024.
accepted.x: The TDF-funded green propulsion system developed by Bellatrix Aerospace was tested in space on PSLV-C58 in January 2024.
accepted.tq: Match the innovation with its developer, launch vehicle and date.
accepted.sec: Technology Development Fund - purpose, cap, projects  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is associated with VIMARSH 2026?
o: Direct funding, incubation and test-facility access for MSMEs and start-ups, along with source-code sharing
Only export financing for large foreign defence manufacturers
A ban on private participation in defence research
Construction of seven DPSUs from Ordnance Factory Board units
accepted.x: VIMARSH 2026 provides direct funding, incubation and access to test facilities for MSMEs and start-ups, and includes source-code sharing.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive package of support measures linked to the initiative.
